findings.evidence: Step 3.1 supplies a finite ball cover of K=Q\\O, but step 3.2 asserts without a bound that its rectangle-volume sum is below eta/2. For a constant integrand S_alpha may be empty and K=Q, so this arbitrary cover cannot have total volume below every eta. Steps 1.3 and 2.2 already cover S_{1/r} by high-oscillation grid cells plus the grid skeleton; converting those rectangles using step 1.1 supplies the needed small cube cover. This assigned consumer directly depends on the published theorem for zero-extension integrability.
